body:
Part of the Omni chat → Agent Bar UX redesign. The Agent Bar is a session-independent surface for directing agents across sessions, so a per-session model picker doesn't belong in it.

## Description

- **Hide the model picker in the Agent Bar** — gate the `OpenModelPickerAction` `MenuId.ChatInput` contribution on `ChatContextKeys.inChatInputWindow.negate()`. This context key is already set to `true` inside the floating input window, so the picker is suppressed there while remaining unchanged in regular chat, inline, notebook, and terminal locations.

```ts
when: ContextKeyExpr.and(
    // Hide the model picker in the Agent Bar (floating chat input window)
    ChatContextKeys.inChatInputWindow.negate(),
    // Hide the model picker while a delegation (continue in) target is pending
    ChatContextKeys.hasPendingDelegationTarget.negate(),
    /* …existing conditions… */
)
```

The toolbar's `actionViewItemProvider` (which builds `ModelPickerActionItem`) only runs for menu items whose `when` clause passes, so no additional cleanup is required.

### Scope

Focused on the concrete "remove the model picker" item. The broader redesign (rename to "Agent Bar" as the product term, voice/attention polish, persisting the bar when the Agents window closes per #331374) is larger and design-led; it's left for follow-ups.

title: agentHost: sync BYOK experiment enablement
body:
## Summary

- Synchronizes the experiment-resolved BYOK setting through agent-host root configuration.
- Makes BYOK models available to model selection and new sessions only when the shared enablement gate allows them.
- Preserves explicit environment overrides and allows setting changes to take effect without restarting the agent host.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

BYOK experiment defaults resolve in the renderer, but the main-process configuration used for launch-time environment variables does not include that experiment layer. The renderer could therefore enable BYOK while the agent host remained disabled.

### Implementation

The BYOK setting now maps to a local-only agent-host root-config key. The typed Agent Host configuration descriptor requires every experiment-backed setting to declare an agent-host mapping.

The renderer keeps the BYOK reverse-RPC channel available for later enablement and registers a no-op channel when the language-model handler is unavailable. A shared gate applies explicit environment overrides before synchronized root config and is used for both model publication and per-session provider/model synthesis.

### Behavior and constraints

- BYOK remains local-only because remote agent hosts cannot access the local extension-host language model API.
- Explicit environment overrides take precedence over synchronized configuration.
- Disabled BYOK models are neither shown in the picker nor added to new session configuration.

</details>

title: Add mute-mic button and transcript quick-toggle to Agents Voice Mode
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4d73178-5957-45f4-89a9-6b7925bc0ccf



## Description

Voice Mode had no way to temporarily silence the microphone without ending the session, and no in-UI control for the live transcript. This adds a persistent mute/unmute button and a per-session transcript toggle.

### Controller (`voiceSessionController.ts`)
- New `isMuted` observable + `setMuted()` on `IVoiceSessionController`.
- While muted, captured audio is dropped at the `onPttAudioChunk` gate so nothing reaches transcription/the backend; the WebSocket stays connected so unmute resumes instantly (no new handshake).
- Mute resets on (re)connect and disconnect.

```ts
this._voiceEventDisposables.add(this.micCaptureService.onPttAudioChunk(b64 => {
    if (this._isMuted.get()) { return; } // keep session alive, drop audio
    this.voiceClientService.sendPttAudioChunk(b64);
}));
```

### UI (`agentsVoiceWidget.ts`, `headerComponent.ts`)
- Mute button rendered in the floating window's input-box toolbar and the classic header. Icon swaps `codicon-mic` ↔ `codicon-mute`, error color + `aria-pressed` when muted, shown only while connected.
- `toggleMute` callback + reactive `setMuted` setter; wired through `agentsVoiceWindowService.ts` and bound from the controller in `agentsVoiceWidgetBinding.ts`.

### Transcript toggle (`micButtonMenuActions.ts`)
- Checkable **"Show Transcript"** entry in the Voice Mode context menu, backed by the existing `agents.voice.showTranscript` setting (the user default, already off by default alongside `agents.voice.liveTranscript`).

### Tests
- Controller test: mute gates outgoing audio while staying connected; unmute resumes.
- Extended mic-button menu test for the new entry.

body:
Cherry-picks 9a882e254de (#331362) to release/1.134.

title: Fix duplicate floating window when adding context in omni chat
body:
## Description

Adding context/attachments in the omni chat input window spawned a second, legacy Quick Chat window near the top of the screen.

**Root cause:** The omni chat widget uses `{ isQuickChat: true }` in its view context (for sizing, titles, etc.). After accepting a pick, `AttachContextAction._show` re-opens the quick chat for any `isQuickChat` widget:

```ts
if (isQuickChat(widget)) {
    quickChatService.open();
}
```

This re-open exists to restore the legacy Quick Chat after the attachment picker hides it — but the omni window's picker lives in its own action-widget window and never hides the omni window, so the call just opened a spurious legacy instance.

**Changes:**
- Added `isChatInputWindow?: boolean` to `IChatResourceViewContext` and an `isChatInputWindow(widget)` helper (alongside `isQuickChat`/`isInlineChat`).
- Tagged both omni chat input window widgets with `isChatInputWindow: true`.
- Guarded the re-open to exclude the omni window:

```ts
if (isQuickChat(widget) && !isChatInputWindow(widget)) {
    quickChatService.open();
}
```

Legacy Quick Chat behavior is unchanged.

title: Match a remote host's working directories against the window's folder
body:
Fixes #330979.

In a remote window every agent session is filtered out of the list.

The store receives each session's working directories wrapped for the agent-host filesystem, and compares them to the window's workspace folder:

```
directory: vscode-agent-host://b64-<encoded host address>/workspace/printstream?_ah=<meta>
folder:    vscode-remote://dev-container%2B<hex>/workspace/printstream
```

`isEqualOrParent` compares schemes before anything else:

```ts
isEqualOrParent(base: URI, parentCandidate: URI, ignoreFragment: boolean = false): boolean {
    if (base.scheme === parentCandidate.scheme) {
```

so the containment check short-circuits to `false` however identical the paths are, and the list comes back empty rather than partial.

### Fix

The wrapper carries the original URI in its `_ah` query, so `fromAgentHostUri` recovers the directory exactly as the host named it. For a host running in a dev container that is the very `vscode-remote:` URI the window uses for that folder: measured in a live window, the unwrapped authority equals the folder's authority byte for byte. Containment then does the rest, so a sibling or a prefix-only lookalike (`/workspace/printstream-2`) still does not match.

This matters beyond making the comparison work. A bare path carries no host identity, so deciding it belongs to the folder's machine can only ever be an assumption. The unwrapped URI carries that identity, so a directory on a *different* remote is rejected on the evidence rather than adopted.

The scheme rewrite stays, narrowed to what it is: the fallback for a host that reports a bare `file:` path with no wrapper to unwrap. It applies only to a `file:` directory against a folder that has an authority, so a local window compares `file:` to `file:` and is untouched, and it is the only part that still assumes this store's single host connection is the folder's machine.

### Verification

- The matching predicate is exported so the tests exercise it rather than a replica. Coverage: the wrapped dev-container pair from the issue, a wrapped directory on a different remote, the bare `file:` fallback, nested and sibling directories, the prefix-only lookalike, the already-remote form, a mismatched authority, and a local window in which nothing is rewritten. The wrapped case fails if the unwrap is removed.
- Verified live in a dev-container window: sessions list, including ones created minutes earlier. Before the fix the same window listed none.

An earlier revision of this PR did the scheme rewrite alone. It does not fix this case, because the reported directory is not `file:` at all, so the rewrite never fires. I am noting that rather than quietly replacing it, since the description above previously claimed otherwise on the strength of host-side logs, which report a directory before the client wraps it.

title: Agents Window: a model picked in the Workbench picker never reaches session.modelId
body:
## Summary

A model picked in the embedded Workbench chat picker never reaches `session.modelId`, so the Sessions picker and the Workbench picker can show different models for the same conversation until something re-syncs. Whichever refreshes last wins.

This is the remaining half of the divergence investigated during #331282. The destructive half — a reopened session being switched to whatever model was last used elsewhere in the profile — is fixed there. This one is not, and is cosmetic rather than corrupting: nothing incorrect is written to the backend, the two surfaces just disagree on screen.

## Evidence

From an `AI debug` window log (agent-host `copilotcli` session `2446d56e…`):

- The user picks GPT‑5.6 in the Workbench picker: `event=explicit-selection surface="workbench" model="agent-host-copilotcli:gpt-5.6-sol"`
- Two minutes later the Sessions side still reports `desiredModel="agent-host-copilotcli:claude-opus-5"` for that same `conversationKey`, while the Workbench side restores `gpt-5.6-sol`.

## Why — the loop is complete except for one link

The wiring already exists end to end. `_inputStateToDraft` (`agentHostSessionHandler.ts:5271`) **already carries the model** out to the host:

```ts
const model = this._createModelSelection(state.selectedModel?.identifier, state.modelConfiguration);
...
...(model ? { model } : {}),
```

| Direction | Path | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Sessions → Workbench | `setModel` → `_updateChatSessionState` → `inputModel.setState` | works |
| Workbench → host draft | picker → `_syncInputStateToModel` → `_installDraftSync` → `ChatState.draft.model` | works |
| host draft → `session.modelId` | `_hydrateModelFromDraft` | **one-shot** |

`_hydrateModelFromDraft` (added in #331282, `baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts`) reads `ChatState.draft.model` but calls `listener.clear()` as soon as `modelId` is defined — copied from `_hydrateAgentFromDraft` beside it, where one-shot is correct. Both subscribe to the same chat channel, so the value genuinely flows; it is simply no longer being observed.

Note this is **not** a `ChatInputPart` problem, which is where I first assumed it lived.

## Proposed fix

Roughly 20–30 lines in `baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts`:

1. Drop the one-shot `listener.clear()` so the observer keeps mirroring
2. Guard on "the draft model differs from the current `modelId`" so a Sessions write echoing back does not loop
3. Record mirrored changes as `ChatModelSource.Restored` — the draft records *what* the conversation runs on, never *who* chose it

## Worth proving, not assuming

- **Echo loop.** Sessions write → input state → draft → observer → `setChatModelId`. The guard must actually break it; worth a test rather than an assumption.
- **Provenance coarsening.** A `User` pick echoing back arrives as `Restored`. Both count as the conversation's own under the precedence rule in `chatInputModelSelectionController.ts`, so no outcome changes — only the label. Same trade already accepted for canonicalized writes in #331282.
- **Asymmetry with the agent**, which stays one-shot. Defensible (the model has a demonstrated bug, the agent does not) but should carry a comment so it reads as deliberate.
- **Cross-client.** A peer changing the draft model would begin moving `session.modelId`. Probably correct — it *is* the conversation's model — but it is a behavior change beyond the logged bug and should be a conscious decision.

## Context

- #331282 shares one model-selection policy between Workbench chat and the Agents Window, and fixes the destructive direction plus the missing model hydration.
- The invariant this would complete is documented in `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md` under "Model selection".

title: Count the session's changes, not the branch's divergence
body:
Fixes #330941.

The session-list chip is computed from the `changeKind: 'branch'` changeset in two places. A branch measures itself against its upstream, so it includes every commit made before the session existed and by everyone else. A session that has never run a turn, and owns no file edits at all, still gets a count.

**The write path** produced the chip during the branch refresh, on this premise:

> SINGLE-folder: derive it from the primary branch `diffs`, exactly as before — that branch changeset IS the whole session footprint.

That premise is the defect. Ownership moves to the `changeKind: 'session'` changeset, which is the session's own footprint.

**The read path** did the same for unopened sessions, and persisted what it derived, making the wrong number durable:

```ts
const liveSession = this._stateManager.getChangesetState(buildBranchChangesetUri(sessionUri));
const liveChanges = computeChangesSummaryFromLiveState(liveSession);
if (liveChanges) {
    this.persistChangesSummary(sessionUri, liveChanges);
    return liveChanges;
}
```

Worth noting the helper it called documents the opposite of what the call site did — "Only the `changeKind: 'session'` entry feeds the summary" — so the contract and the caller already disagreed. That fallback is gone; with no session-scoped evidence the honest rendering is no chip, and the next completed turn writes the real one.

Fixing either half alone does nothing, which is worth knowing before splitting this up: with only the read path fixed, the write path has already persisted the branch number and the read path then serves it faithfully from `META_CHANGES_SUMMARY`. My first attempt at this asserted exactly that and failed on `{"additions":16070,"deletions":634,"files":1}`.

`summariseDiffs` distinguishes "computed, and empty" (a real zero) from "could not compute" (`undefined`), and only the former is written, so the move cannot substitute a misleading `0 files` for a missing chip.

### The trade this makes, explicitly

Session diffs come from checkpoints:

```ts
if (kind === 'session') {
    const latestTurnId = this._latestTurnIdAcrossChats(session);
    if (!latestTurnId) { return undefined; }
```

So a session with no checkpoints — checkpointing disabled, or one that never completed a turn — now shows no chip rather than a wrong one. I believe that is correct, and it is the same principle as the read-path change, but it is a visible behaviour change and I would rather name it than have it found in review.

### Coverage

The characterization test `single-folder summary stays branch-derived (byte-for-byte unchanged)` asserted the old behaviour and is replaced by one asserting the branch refresh no longer writes or persists the chip, while the branch changeset data itself is unaffected.

I did not manage to unit-test the positive half — a session refresh writing the chip — in this suite: it needs a turn on the default chat plus baseline and turn checkpoints, and the turn would not land in `sessionState.turns` through the harness I had. Flagging that gap rather than claiming coverage I do not have.

Multi-folder sessions aggregate every repository's *branch* diff through `_updateMultiFolderChangesSummary`, so they carry the same defect by the same reasoning. Left alone here because the fix is the same decision applied to a more complex path, and this change is easier to review on its own.

### Rebased onto current main

Upstream has since added multi-folder summary ownership, which touches the same block. That work is preserved unchanged:

- The all-folder aggregate for a multi-root session stays on the branch path, exactly as upstream wrote it. This PR still does not change multi-root behaviour.
- The legacy `'diffs'` key and the single-folder summary move to the session path, guarded by `!isMultiRootSession(...)` so the two paths cannot both write the summary.

The characterization test `single-folder summary stays branch-derived` is replaced in place, rather than deleted, by `a branch refresh no longer writes the chip from the branch divergence`. Its premise is the assumption this PR disputes: it reads "the single primary branch diff IS the whole session footprint", which holds only when the session owns its branch. The replacement keeps the same harness and asserts the branch changeset data is still published, so only the chip ownership is withdrawn.

Full unit suite after the rebase: 14705 passing. The 11 failures are pre-existing on main, in the title controller and turn telemetry, which this PR does not touch.

title: Fix omni chat picker anchoring at non-zero zoom levels
body:
## Description

The omni chat action-widget / picker windows (model picker, context pickers, confirmation menus) are hosted in a separate frameless auxiliary window positioned relative to the omni input surface. The positioning math mixed two coordinate systems, so at zoom levels other than 0 (e.g. Ctrl +/- to zoom level 2) the pickers appeared detached from the omni input.

Root cause: `getBoundingClientRect()` reports **CSS px** within the zoomed content, while native window bounds (`getWindowPosition` → Electron `win.getBounds()`) are **device-independent screen px**. 1 content CSS px = `zoomFactor` screen px, so the offsets only lined up at zoom factor 1.

Changes (`chatInputWindowService.ts`, `_openActionWidgetWindow`):

- **Screen positioning** — scale in-content offsets (`sourceTop`, `sourceRight`, `right`-placement `preferredY`) by `getZoomFactor(sourceWindow)` before adding them to native screen bounds.
- **Internal anchor** — anchor the picker against the widget window's content `clientHeight` (CSS px) instead of the device-independent bounds `height`, since the widget window inherits the source window's zoom.

title: Fix hover flicker on omni chat input toolbars
body:
## Description

The omni chat input runs inside a small, frameless auxiliary window with `overflow: hidden`. Custom toolbar hovers can't fit above/below their button, so they get clamped **on top of** the target. Because the tooltip overlays its own button, the mouse `MOUSE_LEAVE`/`MOUSE_OVER` pair toggles the hover on and off in a loop — the flicker seen on the send button.

Changes:

- **`ChatInputPart` toolbars use native tooltips in the omni window** — when `ChatContextKeys.inChatInputWindow` is set, the shared `hoverDelegate` is `nativeHoverDelegate` instead of `createInstantHoverDelegate()`. Native OS tooltips render outside the window bounds and aren't DOM layers over the button, so they can't be clipped or trigger the enter/leave loop. title: agentHost: Speed up rename chat tool
body:
## Summary

- return from `rename_chat` immediately, before session lookup or persistence completes
- retain the targeted session-registry lookup instead of full `listSessions()` enumeration
- run the rename independently in the background and log deferred failures
- share live-session metadata overlay logic between targeted lookup and `listSessions()`

## Performance

Previously, every rename blocked the agent while hydrating and overlaying metadata for every registered session, including provider metadata and per-session database reads, and then persisted the rename before returning.

The tool now returns immediately. Background work performs one indexed session-registry query, uses live in-memory metadata when available, and at most reads provider metadata for the single target session. This removes all asynchronous lookup and persistence work from the agent-facing tool latency while also changing target resolution from work proportional to the total session count to a constant-size lookup.

Since completion happens after the tool returns, deferred failures are logged and the tool/display result describes a requested rename rather than completed persistence.

## Follow-up

The callback-based `ISessionServerToolAccessor` wiring should be cleaned up separately with a dedicated injectable service or tool-handler classes. That architectural refactor will follow in a separate change so this performance fix stays focused.

title: Filter archived (read-only) sessions out of omni chat pending items
body:
Omni chat surfaced archived sessions as pending items, showing an "Archived sessions are read-only." banner and allowing follow-ups to be routed to an archived session.

## Description

The omni pending-chat list in `chatInputWindowService.ts` was built from every `ChatModel` reporting `requestNeedsInput`, without excluding archived ones. When such an item is shown, the omni input calls `widget.setModel(model)` and adopts that read-only session model. Because the omni `ChatWidget` builds its `ChatReadOnlyBanner` with an `undefined` message, it falls back to the banner's default text — `"Archived sessions are read-only."` — and the archived session becomes a routing target.

Other omni paths (routing candidates, `_refreshSessions`, `_loadPendingSessionModels`) already excluded archived sessions; this list was the gap — e.g. a session archived *after* its model was loaded still lingers in `chatService.chatModels`.

- **Exclude read-only models from pending items**: add `.filter(model => !model.isReadOnly.read(reader))` when composing `pendingChats`, so archived sessions are never surfaced, adopted by the omni input, or routed to.

```ts
const pendingChats: IChatInputWindowPendingChat[] = [...this.chatService.chatModels.read(reader)]
    // Archived sessions are read-only, so their pending prompts must not
    // surface in omni: routing must never target them and the omni input
    // must never adopt a read-only model (which shows the read-only banner).
    .filter(model => !model.isReadOnly.read(reader))
    .filter(model => !!model.requestNeedsInput.read(reader) && !this._hasOnlyResolvedPendingTools(model, reader))
```

The banner is driven by `model.isReadOnly` (`chatWidget.ts` `setReadOnly` autorun), so filtering at the source removes both the erroneous banner and the ability to send to archived sessions.

## Notes

No unit test added: the predicate lives inside a service `autorun` closure that isn't instantiated in tests, and the existing `chatInputWindow.test.ts` suite only covers pure helpers.

title: Complete the response for the turn that ended
body:
A turn ending completes the response belonging to whichever turn is current, not the one that ended. When two turns overlap, the outgoing turn closes the incoming turn's response and every progress batch after that is dropped into it — the turn renders empty.

`isCompleteObs` lives on `AgentHostChatSession`, so both completion paths address the session rather than a turn:

```ts
// _handleTurn
this._activeSessions.get(request.sessionResource)?.isCompleteObs.set(true, undefined);
// _trackServerTurnProgress
onTurnEnded: () => chatSession.isCompleteObs.set(true, undefined),
```

`startServerRequest` resets the flag when it creates the next turn's request/response pair, so the outcome depends on which lands first.

**Measured.** I instrumented `startServerRequest`, `appendProgress` and both turn-end paths with logpoints and drove real turns against a dev container, with a host that starts a new turn when one preempts another.

Benign ordering — the preempted turn ends first, the reset lands last, the turn renders:

```
      0ms  clientTurnEnded
    523ms  startServerRequest
   7327ms  appendProgress …(19)
  19602ms  serverTurnEnded
```

Adverse ordering, from the same setup with a tool-heavy turn (twelve read-only Bash calls) instead of plain text:

```
      0ms  startServerRequest
      5ms  clientTurnEnded      <-- closes the response created 5ms earlier
   2882ms  appendProgress …(16 calls, all dropped)
  26199ms  serverTurnEnded
```

That turn's rendered row is the word `Claude` and nothing else. Sixteen progress batches were produced and discarded. Text-only turns leave ~500ms between the two events and never showed the inversion, in-process or over a socket; a turn ending tool calls closes that gap to milliseconds.

The user-visible failure is total and silent: text, tool calls and any question the model asks all vanish. The changeset chip still renders, because changesets are a separate channel subscription, and no stop button appears because the client believes the turn is over.

**The fix** records which turn owns the response when one claims it, and ignores an end signal from any other turn. A response nothing has claimed is still completed by whichever turn ends, so ordinary sequential turns are unaffected.

Overlap is reachable today through the server-initiated turn path, and any change that lets one turn preempt another makes it routine — #330785 is where I hit it.

The rule is extracted as `completionAppliesToResponse` so it can be tested without standing up a chat session, following `unwrapSessionLoadErrorMessage` in the same file.

title: Resolve a client tool to the client that is still there
body:
Fixes #331289.

A client tool call is stamped with an owning `clientId` resolved through `SessionClientToolsModel.ownerOf`. With no caller-supplied preference that resolved to the *first-inserted* contributor, and a window reload connects with a new `clientId` while the departed client's entry can still be present. Every subsequent call was then stamped with a client that had gone away, and failed on arrival:

```
17:14:38.827  chat/toolCallStart      clientId=<old>
17:14:38.830  chat/toolCallComplete   Client <old> disconnected before completing openBrowserPage
17:14:40.646  chat/toolCallComplete   …another active client now provides openBrowserPage. You may try calling the tool again.
```

Three milliseconds from start to failure, and the retry advice cannot be taken: the retry resolves to the same departed client. In the session this came from it was still happening 2 hours 8 minutes after that client disconnected, so it is not the disconnect-grace window elapsing — the tool is dead for the life of the session, and the model eventually concludes the tool itself is broken.

The host is simultaneously right and wrong about this: the "another active client provides it" sentence is guarded by `_hasReplacementActiveClientTool`, which reads `state.activeClients` and correctly sees the live client, while `ownerOf` reads the tool model and answers with the dead one. Two registries, permanently disagreeing.

This makes the resolution self-correcting rather than chasing the disagreement. The model now tracks the most recent contributor and prefers it when the caller expresses no preference. A reconnecting window re-pushes its tool list, so the newest contributor is the one most recently known to be alive; an explicit `preferredClientId` still wins, and removing the latest contributor falls back to whoever remains.

`canRefineContributor` makes this worth fixing at the point of resolution: a client contributor may only be refined by the same client, so once a call is stamped with a departed id nothing downstream can re-point it.

Scope is deliberately narrow — only the Claude path goes through `SessionClientToolsModel`. `codexMapAppServerEvents.ts:748` resolves through `ActiveClientToolSet` directly and has the same shape, but I have not reproduced it there and have left it alone.

Two existing tests asserted the first-inserted default and are updated to the new behaviour, since that default is what produced the bug. Added coverage for the reconnect case itself and for the fallback when the latest contributor is removed.

title: Force the Agent Host harness when the sandbox is managed
body:
## Why

When an enterprise mandates the Copilot SDK sandbox through managed settings, new chats can still use the legacy local harness unless the administrator also configures several harness settings. That makes the sandbox rollout harder to manage and can leave new chats outside the governed Agent Host path.

## What

Treat an effective managed `sandbox.enabled: true`, resolved across native MDM, the server, and the managed-settings file, as the harness governance signal:

- hide the legacy local harness from new-chat pickers
- default new editor and panel chats to the Agent Host Copilot SDK
- apply the decision consistently across the picker, New Chat actions, editor inputs, and the chat panel
- report the managed values and effective decision in `Developer: Policy Diagnostics`

The runtime remains responsible for enforcing the sandbox; this change only selects the appropriate harness and introduces no new VS Code policy.

Existing local sessions continue working. Remembered Claude and Codex selections are preserved, virtual workspaces continue using the local harness, and the existing fallback prevents a window from being left without a usable harness. User or workspace sandbox settings and managed values other than `true` do not trigger this behavior.

## Testing

Added unit coverage for managed-setting channel precedence, managed harness selection, remembered providers, new-chat entry points, unavailable-harness fallback, virtual workspaces, and native managed-setting registration.

title: Fix process memory in `code --status`
body:
Fixes #331296

Related to #194322 and #331139.

## What changed

- Treat `ProcessItem.mem` consistently as bytes when formatting the `code --status` process table.
- Document the byte-valued `ProcessItem.mem` contract.

## Root cause

`listProcesses` already converts non-Windows `%mem` values to bytes, but `DiagnosticsService.formatProcessItem` applied the old percentage-to-bytes calculation a second time on macOS and Linux. This produced impossible values such as 25,332,747,904 MB for a process with about 94 MiB RSS.

The Process Explorer already formats `item.mem` as bytes. This change makes the diagnostics text path consistent with that behavior.

PR #331139 changes the macOS source metric from RSS to physical footprint but continues to store the result in bytes, so the two fixes are compatible and address separate output paths.

## Validation

- Reproduced on VS Code 1.133.0, macOS 26.5.1 arm64.
- TypeScript syntax transpile passed for both changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Confirmed the patch applies cleanly to current `main` at `4ccdb71a3e5`.

title: `code --status` multiplies process memory twice on macOS and Linux
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (the calculation is independent of extensions)

- VS Code Version: 1.133.0 (a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.1, arm64

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run `code --status`.
2. Inspect the `Mem MB` values in the process table.

## Actual result

The command reports impossible process-memory values. In one current sample:

- `code --status`: 25,332,747,904 MB for PID 68258
- `ps` RSS for the same PID: 96,624 KiB (about 94 MiB)

## Root cause

`listProcesses` already normalizes `ProcessItem.mem` to bytes on non-Windows platforms:

```ts
mem: isWindows ? mem : (totalMemory * (mem / 100))
```

However, `DiagnosticsService.formatProcessItem`, which formats `code --status`, still treats `item.mem` as a percentage on macOS and Linux and multiplies it by total system memory again:

```ts
const memory = process.platform === 'win32' ? item.mem : (osLib.totalmem() * (item.mem / 100));
```

The formatter should consistently convert the byte value with `item.mem / ByteSize.MB`.

## Scope

This is adjacent to, but separate from, #194322 and #331139. Those address which memory metric Process Explorer obtains on macOS. This issue concerns the deterministic double conversion in the `code --status` text formatter. PR #331139 continues to provide `ProcessItem.mem` in bytes, so it does not correct this output path.

The same formatter branch is used on Linux, although the reproduction above is from macOS.

title: Agent host: after a client reconnects, new client tool calls are still attributed to the disconnected client and fail immediately
body:
After a client reconnects, client tool calls created *afterwards* are still attributed to the client that went away, and fail on arrival. The session never recovers: every subsequent call to that tool fails the same way for as long as the session lives.

### What happens

In a dev container session, the window reloaded at `16:45:23Z`. The new client `ade2f5ea` initialized and is the only client ever named in `session/activeClientSet` (33 tools) for the rest of the log.

At `17:14:38Z` — half an hour later — a fresh `openBrowserPage` call is announced as belonging to the *old* client:

```
[1786] 17:14:38.827 s2c  chat/toolCallStart      clientId=fbac6cdc…
[1790] 17:14:38.830 s2c  chat/toolCallComplete   Client fbac6cdc-798c-415c-a75e-3a2782d74493 disconnected before completing openBrowserPage
[1798] 17:14:40.646 s2c  chat/toolCallComplete   The client that was running openBrowserPage disconnected, but another active
                                                 client now provides openBrowserPage. You may try calling the tool again.
```

Three milliseconds from start to failure. The model took the advice and retried; every retry was attributed to `fbac6cdc` and failed identically. The same thing was still happening at `18:53:20Z`, **2 hours and 8 minutes after that client disconnected** — so this is not the disconnect-grace window elapsing, it is permanent.

Two calls in the same log carried no `clientId` on their start line and completed normally (`17:10:28`, `18:53:37`). The failure tracks the stale attribution, not the tool.

From the user's side the tool is simply broken, and the model reasonably concludes the same — in this session it gave up and installed Chromium instead, then reported the integrated browser as failing on every call.

### Why it never recovers

`_pendingClientToolCalls` yields each call's owner from `toolCall.contributor.clientId`, and `_completeDisconnectedClientToolCalls` fails the ones whose owner matches a departed client. Nothing re-attributes a *new* call to a live client that provides the same tool.

The host demonstrably knows a live client provides it: the retry sentence is guarded by `_hasReplacementActiveClientTool`, which returns true only when a *different, active* client offers the same tool name. So at the moment of failure the host holds both "this call belongs to a dead client" and "a live client provides this tool", and acts on the first.

Two `chat/toolCallComplete` actions are also dispatched for the same `toolCallId` (~2s apart), which looks wrong independent of the attribution.

### Expected

A client tool call created after its contributor disconnected should be attributed to an active client that provides the tool. Failing that, the retry advice should not be emitted, since retrying cannot succeed — it currently sends the model into a loop that costs a turn and ends in a wrong conclusion about the tool.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a remote or dev container window and start an agent session that uses a client-contributed tool (the integrated browser tools are convenient).
2. Reload the window, so the client reconnects with a new `clientId`.
3. Ask the agent to use that tool.

### Version

- VS Code 1.133.0, commit `a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960`
- Windows 11 client, dev container remote (linux-arm64 server)

**Disclosure:** this agent host is a locally patched build carrying approximations of several of my open PRs (#330683, #330684, #330730, #330746, #330775, #330933). None of them set `contributor.clientId` — the closest, the single-trigger change, only reads `contributor.kind` — and both the attribution and the failure path quoted above are unmodified. But #330933 does change *when* a client tool executes, so it is fair to ask whether it widens the window; I would rather say so than have it discovered later. The log evidence above is from that build.
